Requirement: As a game platform operator, I want the system to respond to API calls within 2 seconds for 95% of requests and within 4 seconds for the remaining requests, so that players experience smooth, uninterrupted gameplay.
As a business analyst, I want to generate any report and export it with a single button click, so that I can quickly obtain insights without manual steps.
As an audit user, I want the recycled‑parts audit report to be delivered within 10 seconds of request, so that I can verify compliance in a timely manner.
As an end‑user, I want standard menus and buttons for navigation, so that I can use the application intuitively without training.
As a support engineer, I want the product to create an exception log and securely transmit it to our central analysis service, so that issues can be diagnosed and resolved quickly.
As a lead management system, I want leads with a low‑average score to be automatically returned to the supplying vendor, so that the vendor can re‑evaluate or re‑assign those leads.
As a platform scalability engineer, I want the system to handle a large number of concurrent game sessions by scaling horizontally, so that service remains available during peak demand.
As a formulation engineer, I want substitutionary ingredients to be entered automatically by the PFE microservice, so that product formulas are created accurately and efficiently.
As a meeting coordinator, I want the system to record and categorize different meeting types, so that we have accurate records for reporting and analysis.
As a front‑end developer, I want the web UI to support legacy browsers (IE 5‑6, Netscape 6‑8, Firefox 1) so that users on outdated systems can still access the application.
As a game engine, I want to compute each player's status after both have positioned their five ships so that the first turn can start correctly.
As a security officer, I want the CampusConnect integration endpoints to be accessible only to authenticated and authorized users so that sensitive data is protected.
As a solution architect, I want the system to be built following corporate architecture guidelines so that it aligns with enterprise governance and standards.
As a game developer, I want the application to play a sinking ship sound effect when a ship is destroyed so that players receive immersive audio feedback.
As a property seeker, I want clear, high‑resolution property images in search results so that I can evaluate listings quickly.

As a financial planner, I want new branches, districts, and revenue/expense accounts from the BDW to be automatically loaded into the RFS system before the budget start so that budgeting uses complete and up‑to‑date data.
As a UI designer, I want the product to support custom theming with the customer's logo, branding, and identity so that the interface reflects the client’s corporate image.
As a support agent, I want to view follow‑up actions for a dispute case filtered by the case status and my access level so that I can take appropriate next steps.
As a consumer, I want to stream a purchased movie via a compatible player for up to 48 hours after purchase so that I can watch the content on demand within the allowed window.

As a security architect, I want the API gateway to enforce OAuth2 Authorization Code flow with PKCE and must reject requests lacking a valid JWT, so that we reduce the risk of credential leakage and meet compliance requirements.

As a platform engineer, I want the authentication service to provide an immediate revocation endpoint that shall invalidate issued JWTs on logout or compromise, so that compromised sessions cannot be reused.

As a product owner, I want the token issuance component to issue access tokens that must expire within 15 minutes and be refreshed via a rotating refresh token, so that the attack surface is minimized.

As a microservice developer, I want each service to validate the JWT audience and scopes and shall reject tokens with mismatched claims, so that only authorized services can access protected resources.

As a DevOps engineer, I want the OAuth2 token endpoint to require mutual TLS authentication and must verify client certificates, so that only trusted clients can obtain tokens even inside the corporate network.
As a security operations analyst, I want a token introspection endpoint that shall return token status and associated claims in real time, so that we can enforce zero‑trust policies dynamically.

As a compliance officer, I want the authentication service to emit immutable audit logs for every token issuance, refresh, and revocation and must include source IP and client ID, so that we can investigate incidents and satisfy audit requirements.

As a backend engineer, I want the API layer to enforce claim‑based access control that shall verify role, department, and risk level claims in each JWT, so that access decisions follow zero‑trust principles.

As a site reliability engineer, I want the JWT verification library to support automatic key rotation via JWKS and must fallback to previous keys during rotation, so that we maintain continuous service availability while enhancing security.

As a front‑end developer, I want the authentication front‑end to store refresh tokens in HTTP‑only, SameSite=Strict cookies that must be sent only over secure channels, so that token leakage via XSS or CSRF is prevented.
As a Site Reliability Engineer, I want the OpenTelemetry collector to must forward latency metrics to the alerting engine in real time, so that we can detect SLA breaches instantly.
As a Platform Engineer, I want the alerting service to shall attach OpenTelemetry trace identifiers to every incident notification, so that engineers can quickly jump to the root cause.
As an Incident Commander, I want a real‑time error‑budget dashboard that must update every 30 seconds, so that we can decide when to trigger a mitigation runbook.
As a Product Owner, I want the OpenTelemetry alerting engine to shall allow dynamic SLA rule updates through a REST API, so that business can adjust thresholds without code changes.
As a DevOps Engineer, I want the telemetry ingestion layer to must implement back‑pressure throttling, so that alert generation remains reliable under load spikes.
As a QA Engineer, I want the incident alerting system to shall collapse duplicate alerts that share an OpenTelemetry trace ID, so that on‑call engineers receive a single actionable notification.
As a Security Analyst, I want all generated alerts to be logged to an immutable store that must retain the full OpenTelemetry context, so that we can audit incident handling for regulatory purposes.

As a Customer Support Lead, I want the self‑service portal to shall display each tenant's live error‑budget usage derived from OpenTelemetry metrics, so that customers can monitor their own SLA compliance.

As a Data Engineer, I want a streaming export job that must deliver OpenTelemetry trace data to the analytics lake within 5 seconds of collection, so that predictive SLA breach models stay up‑to‑date.
As a Cloud Architect, I want the OpenTelemetry agents to shall automatically attach cost‑center tags to every metric, so that we can correlate SLA violations with financial impact.
